findings.comment: No certified food protection manager (CFM) is present at the facility. There should be a CFM present at all times food or drinks are being served. findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the basin of the kitchen hand-sink to be obstructed by a cardboard box at the start of the inspection. findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: During the start of the inspection the sanitizer buckets were observed to have a concentration of 0 ppm quaternary ammonia, and the sanitizer at the triple sink contained 50 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- food handler remade sanitizer buckets and sanitizer water at the triple sink to be within the desired concentration (200-400 ppm). Ensure sanitizer is changed at a frequency to obtain the required concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Two gallons of milk in the counter cooler were observed to not contain any date marking. When the inspector asked the person in charge (PIC) when the milk was opened, they stated it was opened yesterday. CORRECTED-PIC placed a date on both containers of milk. Ensure that items that are not used within the day of service are marked with the date they were first opened, and used or discarded within seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Hand sanitizer was used in place of handwashing prior to baking cookies. Hands were unable to be properly washed due to the absence of water at the facility while the sprinkler system was in the process of being tested. Staff were advised on handwashing and to cease all operations until water is available to allow for proper handwashing. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:

Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Employee began baking cookies while facility did not have water. Cookies were discarded upon removal from the oven.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 Previously observed evidence of rodent activity was not present. A few new droppings were observed under the oven counter along the east wall. Staff confirmed the small hole at the bottom of the east wall as the location of rodent harborage based on observations made after cleaning occurred. Facility is working with PCO to resolve the issue. PCO was out on 5/23/22 and will be out again some time next week for additional service. Ensure traps are placed along the east wall near the harborage location. **See general comments for additional information**
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Commercially processed snack packs containing Genoa salami and Fontina cheese were observed with surface temperatures of 55F-64F. Label on package stated to keep refrigerated. Packages were stacked in three paperboard displays on the top shelf on the refrigerated side of the display cooler. Internal temperatures were observed at 54F-62F depending on where packages were stacked within the display. A lone package on the shelf behind the paperboard displays had an internal temperature of 44F. All packages in the display cooler were discarded. Cooler was holding below 41F, and all other foods had surface and internal temperatures below 41F. ** See general comments for additional information**
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

Gnawed, empty oyster cracker packages were observed on the counter behind the oven and behind the soup warmer. findings.citation_text:

Store manager and all staff that have the potential to work in the food service area need to read and sign a copy of the employee health reporting agreements. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Store manager stated company did not have a written policy for responding to vomit and/or diarrhea incidents. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided. Handout has directions for use of bleach during disinfection. Facility currently has Peroxide Multi-surface Cleaner and Disinfectant available, which is also effective against Norovirus. Ensure a policy is established and available for use based on the product that will be used for disinfection in case of a vomit and/or diarrhea incident.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06  Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. Proof of food handler certification was not available staff working in the cafe at the time of inspection. All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site. New hires have 30 days from the date of hiring to complete food handler training. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Cafe manager has a food handler certification but is in the process of getting a food manager certification. None of the staff currently have a food manager certification. (see general comments for details).

Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Cups of water and coffee were observed on a storage shelf with tea and other items in the kitchen across from the ice machine. Manager was advised on providing an area for drink storage that will promote handwashing after consumption. Personal drinks were moved to a shelf separate from food and equipment above the back handsink. 

Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee's hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee left the service area to get the manager. Upon returning to the cafe the employee did not wash hands prior to waiting on customers, working the register, and preparing beverages. Handwashing was discussed, and employee was later observed washing hands between tasks. Educational handout on when to wash hands was provided.

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon entering the work area and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-buckets was at 0ppm. Upon preparing new solutions it was discovered the sanitizer was not suctioning through the chemical line of the wall mounted dispenser properly. The bottle hooked up to the dispenser did not have the proper tubing within the bottle. Manager replaced the chemical bottle with one that had the proper tubing in the product, and the suction issue was resolved. New solutions were prepared and observed at 200mppm. 

A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain quat solutions at 200-400ppm as directed by the label instructions.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 Timer used as indicator for rotating time controlled carafes of half and half was not set when the in-use carafe was placed in the self-service area for customers. Manager noted each carafe has a label indicating the 4hr time frame for use and a timer is used to let staff know when the product is to be changed. Carafe had time of 1-5 on it. Make sure the appropriate timer is also set so staff know without a doubt when to switch product, especially as shift changes occur. (see general comments for additional details)

If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control and served or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Wiping cloth for the espresso wand was observed sitting on the machine by the wand and not stored in sanitizer solution between uses. Proper storage of wiping cloths between uses was discussed. Wiping cloth in question was discarded and replaced with a fresh cloth when the solution was changed. 

Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Box of cups was observed on the ground between the back handsink and 3 part sink in the cafe. Also, several boxes of single use articles and food items were observed on the floor in the back storage hallway. Store all food and food related single use articles up off the floor. 

Food, single service, and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 A leak was observed at a pipe under the ice machine. Repair the pipe according to the Illinois and local plumbing codes.

A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floors were soiled in the cafe under equipment, especially at the front service area, and in the back storage area under cooler and freezers. Clean the floors throughout.

Dust accumulation was observed on the ceiling vent covers above the door to the cafe. Clean the vent covers. 

Dish machine had some of soap powder and splash on general surfaces. Clean the general surfaces of the dish machine.

Three part sink basins, especially the middle compartment, and the drains boards were soiled. Clean the 3 part sink basins and drain boards.

Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-501.110 Employees personal belongings (vaping device, keys, cell phone) were observed on storage shelving in the cafe across from the ice machine. Proper storage was discussed, and all items were removed from the cafe. 

Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.153 - Half and half in a carafe at the self service counter had an internal temperature 48°F. Store manager noted time control is used for the product. A label was not present on the carafe to indicate time frame for use. Employee working at the time started his shift at 11a and was not informed by the person working prior as to what time the half and half was put out. Remaining half and half would be used or discarded by 1p.
Make sure time is tracked for the half and half, either directly on the carafe or somewhere in back where staff can keep track and ensure proper use/discard.

When using time as a control, food shall be marked to indicate the time when it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.280 - Spoon for dried strawberries was observed with the handle down in the product. Spoon was repositioned so the handle was up out of product. Storage options for spoon were discussed.

Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food, clean and dry, or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee left the food service area to get the store manager and did not wash hands upon returning. Employee was also observed going between tasks and handling money without washing hands prior to preparing orders.
Another employee that was called to help when a rush occurred did not wash her hands upon entering the food service area. 
Proper handwashing between tasks and upon entering the food service area was discussed. Manager was advised to reiterate the importance of handwashing with all staff. Educational handout on when to wash hands was provided.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time they may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and single service articles.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Open can of Red Bull was observed in the bottom of the 2 door cooler at the food service area. Drink was discarded. Manager stated staff have an area in the break room for storage of personal food/beverage.

Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Quat test strips had an expiration date of 2014 and did not appear to be registering properly when used. Test strips were discarded. Manager stated test strips would be ordered today.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Wiping cloth used for espresso wand was not in sanitizer solution between uses. Sanitizer solution was provided.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Back handsink was blocked by a cart and step stool. The handsink itself was soiled with stuck on buildup, had scrubber pads in the basin, and did not have paper towels stocked in the dispenser. All items were removed from the area around the sink. The handsink was cleaned and properly stocked during inspection.

Handsinks shall be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Spray bottle with a sanitizer/disinfectant label had what appeared to be a corrosive powder cleaner inside (product separated out/smelled like Comet cleaner). Manager was unsure what was in the bottle. chemical was discarded during the inspection. 

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.citation_text:
750.540 - Facility does not currently have a certified food manager to oversee operations. Store manager will be getting her certification. The need for multiple certified food managers was discussed (see general comments). 

Category II facilities must have enough certified food managers to oversee operations at the facility and help ensure proper food handling.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Some debris accumulation was present in the bottom of the ice scoop holder. Manager noted the holder is on a weekly cleaning schedule. Manager was advised the holder should be cleaned and sanitized more frequently dependent upon soil. Holder was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection.

Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - Plastic ice scoop was observed with a cracks along the bottom of the food contact surface and around the handle. Replace the ice scoop.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) behind Toastmaster baking oven & sliders under legs (dust/crumbs);
B) under/behind espresso machine (dust/general buildup);   and
C) bottom inside freezer in back storage room (debris accumulation).

Clean general surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
750.1060 - Back handsink filled ~1/3 full of water when inspector washed hands and was very slow draining. Manager plunged the sink and cleared out a bottle cap that got lodged down in the drain. The sink began to drain properly.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.
findings.citation_text:
750.1100 - Water filtration drain line was observed discharging water on the floor next to the drain under the ice machine. Adjust the drain line so it dispenses into the floor drain.

Drain lines from equipment shall not discharge waste water in such a manner as will permit the flooding of floors or the flowing of water across working or walking areas or into difficult-to-clean areas, or otherwise create a nuisance.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floors were soiled in the following areas:
A) under the ice machine (general debris & moisture);
B) under cooler and freezers in back room (general debris);  and
C) under freezers and cooler in back storage area (debris & splash accumulation).

Floors shall be maintained clean. Clean the floors under equipment daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: 750-290 Observed the blue bucket holding the ice scoop to be soiled. Clean the ice storage container. Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510d Observed an employee improperly washing their hands. Hands were washed and then clean hands were used to turn off the faucets. Use a barrier to turn off the soiled faucet. Wash hands, dry them, and then use the paper towel to turn off the faucet.  To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b The two sani-buckets on the frontline are observed at 0ppm and 100ppm quat. The buckets were refilled during the inspection. Monitor the sani-buckets and refill as needed to maintain at 200ppm Quat throughout the day. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed the interior of the coolers in the backroom to be soiled with food splash and crumbs. Clean the interior of the coolers.  Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 The kitchen is still in excellent repair, however, several of the hinges on the cabinet doors are loose. Watch the doors of the cabinets along the backline especially under the Turbo Chef as the hinges are pulling from the cabinet bases. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 750-1100(b) Observed the drain line from the preparation sink to have a cup attached to the end flowing into the floor drain. The drain was previously a source of ponding floor water. Eliminate the use of a cup and provide a proper air gap. Plumbing has been addressed twice this year and another repair is scheduled. The pipes keep moving away from the floor drain and result in ponding water. Repair plumbing so that there is not a cup in-use, so that an air gap is evident, and so no water ponds on the floor. Cup was removed during the inspection. Drain lines from equipment shall not discharge waste water in such a manner as will permit the flooding of floors or the flowing of water across working or walking areas or into difficult-to-clean areas, or otherwise create a nuisance.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: 750-1120(b) The handsink in the back room is covered with boxes. Moved during the inspection. Make sure that hand sinks are accessible at all times. There is much to do in this small kitchen and availability of handsinks allows for easy handwashing between tasks. Also, discussed with employee the need to wash hands before wearing gloves. Every time a task is switched (taking money, handling chemicals, to handling food hand should be washed).  Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 The floor behind the microwave by the display cooler is observed soiled with accumulated food crumbs and dust. Pull out the microwave cart and clean the floor. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: 750-1390 Observed the mop head stored with head into mop basin. Store mop hanging or over the mop bucket to allow wet mop head to properly drip dry. Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540 There is currently no certified food manager working in this facility. Previous manager had to let his certificate lapse. The cafe has just hired a new manager. She will be on-site within a week at which point a certificate may be available. Should manager have certification then please provide a copy of the certificate. Should manager not have certification, then see that the proper coursework is completed and money sent to IDPH for a proper FSSM certificate.  All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 690: See previous report for details.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: 1120b: See previous report for details. There is only one sink present on the frontline. Facility was storing coffee pots witihin the sink during the inspection. A work order has been submitted (requesting an additional sink be installed, counter will support a double basin). Facility needs a 'dump' sink and a handwashing sink available on the frontline. Pots are filled and dumped regularly throughout the day. Inspected during busy lunch period and two employees are busy providing all services expected from a barista (coffee drinks, cash collection, and food service too).

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-130(c) Juice bottles are observed stored beneath the drainline of the frontline handsink. Cease storing these beverages beneath the handsink drain. There is sufficient room to allow for a foot clearance beneath the drainline and still have ample storage for the beverages. Think veritcal - there is room for shelving to allow for stacked beverage storage to the side of this drainline. Food shall not be stored under sewer lines or water lines.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 The cabinets of the frontline display cooler have become quite rusted. White paint is beginning to chip from the shelves - especially along the back portion where employees constantly draw plates of food. Seal the shelves. Also, see the notes in General Comments. The cabinets are observed with spray foam filling holes. Holes have been filled to prevent pests from traveling between the cabinetry. Cut spray foam flush and seal the foam to create a nonabsorbent, easily cleanable surface. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) The ice deflector within the bulk ice machine is observed with a small amount of black mold growth. Clean and sanitize this baffle. To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The muffin freezer and the milk cooler within the back room are observed soiled. Milk cooler has a old milk smell from broken gallon spill. Clean these two cold holding units. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: 750-1120(b) There is only one sink available at the frontline. This sink is the designated handsink. The handsink available in the backroom is too far from the service area to serve as their frontline handsink. This frontline handsink is also being used as a dump sink. During the inspection, the sink was used to wash hands, rinse out pots, and empty various beverages. During the inspection, discussed using this sink solely for handwashing. Place a bucket and a colander as a temporary dump sink. Empty and was temporary dump sink daily. This facility is in need of a two part sink where this large single basin frontline hadnwashing sink is located. A two part sink will allow for all needs of food code and baristas to be met.  Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 750-1160 Evidence of a recent pest problem is still present in two sets of cabinets (manager is aware of location). Clean up the mouse droppings within these cabinets. The source has already been eliminated. See violation #15 as well. Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. See last routine for details.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.  See last routine for details.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: The cold case had been turned off over night and so it went into a defrost cycle in the middle of the afternoon instead of 2am. Potentially hazardous foods are not stored in the glass case over night. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above). Cooler is now running at 38F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Areas under the bank of cabinets in the front are raw and no longer easily cleansable. 750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleansable. Seal or paint the cabinet shelves and edges so that they are easily cleansable.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The following non food contact areas are soiled: 1) shelves in cold case 2) inside of cabinets in front.750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Utensils observed stored in green caddy under oven with crumbs and dust and knives and serving utensils are stored on top of microwave in container with crumbs and dust. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Properly clean utensils and holders and maintain clean.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: Single use utensils are stored in caddy that is soiled with crumbs and dust up under front counter. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law. Clean container and maintain clean so that the utensils are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: The hand sink is blocked in the back. 750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times. Do not  block the hand sink. Binders blocking the hand sink were removed.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: The garage door in the back storage area has light visible under it. 750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects. Replace brushes so that the entrance of insects and rodents is deterred.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. There are cardboard boxes used to hold sandwiches in the coolers and freezers. If the sandwiches came in those boxes they can be used but should be changed out with each new supply. Use only smooth easily cleansable materials for storage of items that do not come in boxes. Some of the shelves inside the back counter at front line are in disrepair. Repair or replace these shelves.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. The following non-food contact items are soiled: 1) track of glass front cooler 2) bottom of far right hand side cooler in dish area and 3) cart shelf holding syrup bottles. Clean and keep clean.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects. The front doors have a considerable gap between them and some areas where light can be seen across bottom of door. Openings to the outside shall be tight fitting and self closing. Repair the doors.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. There is some soil on the floors especially in difficult to reach areas and around the soda drain. Clean the floors and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 810b: Observed a damp blue wiping cloth used at the espresso machine to be stored on top of the machine or on the counter.  In-use wiping cloths shall be stored in the bucket of sanitizing solution when not in use.  The wiping cloth was placed in the bucket during inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 800e:  Observed the inside of cabinet under the soda machine to be soiled.  Clean the inside of the cabinet under the soda machine.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 1060: Observed the faucet on the mopsink to leak when turned on and to be without a cold water handle.  Repair the faucet on mopsink so that it has working cold water with a handle and so the faucet does not leak while on or off.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1220a: Observed dust accumulation on the two ceiling vents above the ice machine in the back kitchen area.  Clean the ceiling vents above the ice machine in back kitchen area.

(Next Remodel of Facility) 1210a:Ceiling tiles over the service area are acoutic tiles.  At next remodel of facility, replace ceiling tiles with tiles that are non-absorbant, smooth, and easily cleanable.  The ceiling tiles in the back kitchen area over the sinks and ice machine are correct tiles.
